chunks: And as for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who has a Christian wife, and she converts to Islam; is it permissible for her to remain with him? He said, 'If she converts, she is not permissible to him.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, but the husband converted after that; are they still on the marriage?' He said, 'No, with a new marriage.'

And this does not contradict the first report, because this report is applied to one who has left the conditions of the Dhimma. If his state is as we mentioned and his wife converts, then he is awaited for the duration of her waiting period; if he converts, he is more entitled to her, and if he does not convert, she has been separated from him.
And that which indicates that whenever they fail in the conditions of the Dhimma, their Dhimma is invalidated, is what has been narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a Christian wife and her Muslim husband if he remains a non-Muslim?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Rida clarifies the fiqh of mixed-faith marriages upon conversion, distinguishing between the immediate separation when the wife converts while the husband remains non-Muslim and the requirement for a new contract if the husband subsequently converts. The text further explains that this ruling applies specifically to those who retain the conditions of *Dhimma*; if they abandon these conditions, their status changes, reinforcing the principle that apostasy or change in religious status invalidates the existing marital bond.
